duplicate_changed_state.label: Stripe docs › Webhooks › Handle duplicate events · Retry behavior

accepts_tampered.title: Accepts tampered payload
accepts_tampered.what: {d} changed {tamper.path} from {tamper.from} to {tamper.to} and was signed for the original body. Your handler returned {status} in {latency_ms} ms[[probe|: {probe} {before} → {after}]], expected a 4xx and no change.
accepts_tampered.why: Stripe signs the exact bytes it sends. If a failed check doesn't stop the request, anyone who can reach this URL can make your handler act on content Stripe never sent.
accepts_tampered.fix: Return 400 as soon as signature verification fails, before any write. After the fix, {d} should get 400[[probe| and leave {probe} at {before}]].

accepts_unsigned.title: Accepts a delivery without a signature
accepts_unsigned.what: {d} had no Stripe-Signature header. Your handler returned {status} in {latency_ms} ms[[probe|: {probe} {before} → {after}]], expected a 4xx and no change.
accepts_unsigned.why: Anyone who can reach this URL can send events Stripe never sent.
accepts_unsigned.fix: Reject a request without a signature header with 400, before any write. After the fix, {d} should get 400.

accepts_stale.title: Accepts a stale signature
accepts_stale.what: {d} was signed for a timestamp {timestamp_age_s} s old (tolerance {tolerance_s} s). Your handler returned {status} in {latency_ms} ms[[probe|: {probe} {before} → {after}]], expected a 4xx and no change.
accepts_stale.why: Replay protection relies on the timestamp tolerance: without it, a captured request can be sent again at any time.
accepts_stale.fix: Check the signed timestamp against the tolerance and return 400 when it is outside. After the fix, {d} should get 400.

duplicate_changed_state.title: Duplicate delivery changed {probe} again
duplicate_changed_state.what: The same {event_type} event was delivered again and every response was a 2xx, but {state_list}. Only the probe could see this.
duplicate_changed_state.why: Stripe may deliver the same event more than once, and retries failed or timed-out deliveries with backoff for up to 3 days in live mode. Each duplicate repeats the write.
duplicate_changed_state.fix: Record event.id before the write and return 200 early when it is already recorded. After the fix, {offending} should leave {probe} at {expected}.

order_changed_state.title: Out-of-order delivery left a different state
order_changed_state.what: After the events arrived in reverse order, {probe} was {after}; in capture order it was {expected}.
order_changed_state.fix: Make each event's write depend on the event's own data or the current object, not on arrival order. After the fix, {d} should leave {probe} at {expected}.

concurrent_changed_state.title: Concurrent deliveries left a different state
concurrent_changed_state.why: Stripe sends related events close together, often concurrently.
concurrent_changed_state.fix: Put a unique constraint or a lock around the check-then-insert. After the fix, the burst should leave {probe} at {expected}.

partial_side_effect.title: Failed delivery kept its write
partial_side_effect.why: Stripe retries a failed delivery, so the write happens again.
partial_side_effect.fix: Run the work in a transaction and roll back when it fails. After the fix, {d} should leave {probe} at {before}.

retry_diverged.title: Retry didn't do the work
retry_diverged.what: {d} retried {d_ref}, which failed, and left {probe} at {after}, expected {expected}.
retry_diverged.why: Stripe retries failed deliveries; the retry must do the work the failed attempt didn't.
retry_diverged.fix: Record the event id only after the work commits. After the fix, {d} should leave {probe} at {expected}.

server_error.title: Server error on a valid {event_type} delivery
server_error.what: {d} got {status_text} for a correctly signed {event_type} event.
server_error.why: Stripe counts the delivery as failed and retries it. An endpoint that keeps failing for several days is disabled.
server_error.fix: Find the error for {d} in your handler logs and return a 2xx for valid events. After the fix, {offending} should get a 2xx.

non_2xx_on_valid.title: Rejects a valid {event_type} delivery
non_2xx_on_valid.what: {d} got {status} for a correctly signed {event_type} event.
non_2xx_on_valid.why: Stripe counts a 3xx or 4xx as a failed delivery and retries it. An endpoint that keeps failing for several days is disabled.
non_2xx_on_valid.fix: Return 200 for event types you don't handle, and a 2xx once the event is accepted. After the fix, {offending} should get a 2xx.

error_on_invalid.title: Server error on an invalid delivery
error_on_invalid.what: {d} was built to fail verification and got {status_text}, not a 4xx.
error_on_invalid.why: A 5xx makes Stripe retry and counts toward disabling the endpoint. A failed signature check should be a 400.
error_on_invalid.fix: Return 400 when verification fails, before any other work. After the fix, {d} should get 400.

over_budget.title: Over the {budget_s} s budget for Stripe
over_budget.what: {slow_count} of {valid_count} valid {event_type} deliveries took longer than the {budget_s} s budget ({budget_source}): {latency_list}. Stripe doesn't publish its timeout, so these are over our default budget, not proven failures at Stripe.
over_budget.why: If Stripe times out waiting, the delivery counts as failed and is retried. Stripe doesn't publish the timeout.
over_budget.fix: Acknowledge with 200 first, then queue the slow work. After the fix, {offending} should respond within the budget.

needs_probe.title: State not checked
needs_probe.what: Responses were checked, but without a probe the run can't see duplicate or out-of-order side effects.
needs_probe.why: Most webhook bugs change state, not the response.
needs_probe.fix: Add a probe to webhooktrap.yml. The next run then checks state.

order_dependent.title: No reset between scenarios
order_dependent.what: Without a reset hook each scenario starts from the previous one's state, so comparisons with the baseline can't be judged.
order_dependent.why: Order, retry and burst checks compare against the state one clean delivery leaves.
order_dependent.fix: Add reset: to webhooktrap.yml with a command that empties the tables your handler writes.

probe_gap.title: Probe doesn't see {object_type} state
probe_gap.what: {event_type} was delivered in {scenario_list} ({offending}), and no probe reads {object_type} state.
probe_gap.why: Out-of-order delivery usually breaks status fields, not counts.
probe_gap.fix: Add a {object_type} entry to the probe in webhooktrap.yml. The next run then checks both.

cold_start.title: Slow first delivery
cold_start.what: D1 took {latency_ms} ms, later deliveries ≤ {max_other_ms} ms. Likely a cold start, such as a dev server compiling the route. Not counted.
cold_start.why: Development servers compile the route on the first request.
cold_start.fix: Nothing to fix if your production server is warm.

async_write.title: State changed after the response
async_write.what: {probe} changed 1 s after the last response. Your handler probably writes in a background job.
async_write.why: A reading taken right after the response can miss a background write.

likely_cause.LC-1: Late ({d_ref}) was rejected, so the timestamp check runs; the signature check probably fails into a log line instead of stopping the request.
likely_cause.LC-2: Neither the signature nor the timestamp stops the request: verification is probably missing, or its result is ignored.
likely_cause.LC-3: The signature is checked but the timestamp isn't. This happens when the HMAC is verified by hand, or the tolerance is set very high.
likely_cause.LC-4: Only some deliveries of {event_type} were slow, so the slow step is intermittent: usually an external call or a lock wait before the response.
likely_cause.LC-5: Most deliveries of {event_type} were slow, so the slow work runs before the response on every request.
likely_cause.LC-6: The handler rejects an event that arrives before the record it updates.
likely_cause.LC-7: The same event succeeded in order, so the crash depends on arrival order or concurrency, not on the payload.
likely_cause.LC-8: The handler doesn't record the event id before it writes.
likely_cause.LC-9: Order alone is fine, so concurrent requests race: a check-then-insert without a unique constraint or a lock.
likely_cause.LC-10: The handler writes before the step that fails, and doesn't roll back.

over_budget.express:
res.sendStatus(200);            // acknowledge first
await queue.add('handle-event', { eventId: event.id });

probe_gap.webhooktrap.yml:
probe:
  # keep your existing entries, then add:
  - as: subscriptions.status
    cmd: psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select status from subscriptions where stripe_id = '{{subscription.id}}'"
